answer: To resist Sybils, every agent must anchor its key with a discrete, non-fungible capital stake before issuing claims. Each identity commits time-locked collateral that matures slowly like a vine, capping maximum voting weight per key. If an attacker spins up clones to manufacture a plume of consensus, each identity demands a full, unshareable bond. Misbehavior shatters the bond like cracking a walnut shell, burning the deposit. The scarce cost is the unshareable opportunity cost of capital per key, strictly bounding influence so that N clones cost N times as much with zero payoff.
